key_insight: This paper exactly characterizes the best univariate two-layer ReLU classifiers under minimal norm and logistic regularization, showing how the solution changes depending on whether hidden-layer biases are penalized. In the unpenalized-bias case, the optimal classifier is a continuous piecewise-affine function that tightly follows every label change.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of a complete, geometric understanding of globally optimal solutions for simple ReLU classifiers trained with minimal-norm interpolation or l2-regularized logistic loss, especially under different parameter-norm choices for hidden-layer biases.
method: Analyze univariate two-layer ReLU networks in function space rather than only parameter space.
Derive exact geometric characterizations of minimal-norm interpolators and regularized logistic-loss minimizers.
Compare two regimes: hidden-layer biases included in the norm versus biases left unpenalized.
impact: This gives practitioners a precise picture of what these networks learn in the simplest setting, helping clarify optimization behavior, regularization effects, and the role of bias parameters. The results can guide model design and interpretation in ReLU-based classification.
visual_elements: Side-by-side plot of data points and the exact piecewise-affine classifier
Diagram comparing penalized vs unpenalized hidden biases
Geometry sketch showing label switches and how the optimal function hugs them
Flowchart of the two optimization settings: interpolation and l2-regularized logistic loss
paper_title: Minimal-Norm Univariate Two-Layer ReLU Classification: Exact Solutions and Global Optimality with Skip Connections
paper_authors: Karolina Drabik, Ben Lewis, Antoni Puch, Etienne Boursier, Piotr Hofman
